title: RC Time Constant and Exhalation
subtitle: Observe how expiratory airway resistance affects expiratory time constant and breath-end flow

patient.summary: Intubated patient receiving volume-controlled ventilation under deep sedation following surgery.

prediction.question: When expiratory resistance is increased from 10 to 40 cmH2O/(L/s) at the same respiratory rate and tidal volume, how will auto-PEEP, end-expiratory flow magnitude, and peak airway pressure change?

whatToLookAtHint: Observe the expiratory flow waveform just prior to the next breath trigger and compare the end-expiratory pressure values.

reflection.question: Why does increasing expiratory airway resistance lead to intrinsic PEEP (auto-PEEP) at a respiratory rate of 16 bpm?

options.text: The expiratory time constant (RC) increases, requiring longer expiratory time (3-5 RC) than the ventilator cycle allows, leaving gas trapped when the next breath initiates.
The inspiratory valve opens prematurely due to increased patient trigger sensitivity.
High resistance directly causes alveolar hyperrecruitment and increases static compliance.
Tidal volume automatically doubles to compensate for higher expiratory resistance.

reflection.explanation: The passive expiratory time constant is RC = R_exp × C_rs. At baseline (10 cmH2O/(L/s) × 0.05 L/cmH2O = 0.5 s), exhalation is 95% complete in 3 time constants (1.5 s), well within the available expiratory time (2.75 s). Increasing resistance to 40 cmH2O/(L/s) increases the time constant to 2.0 s. Complete exhalation now requires 6 to 10 seconds. Because exhalation is interrupted at 2.75 s while flow is still exiting the lung, gas remains trapped, generating intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure (auto-PEEP).

evidence.claim: Expiratory time constant (RC) governs passive lung emptying; incomplete exhalation occurs when expiratory time is less than 3 to 5 time constants.
evidence.source: Tobin MJ. Principles and Practice of Mechanical Ventilation. 3rd ed. McGraw-Hill; 2012.

evidence.claim: End-expiratory flow on the flow-time scalar indicates intrinsic PEEP and dynamic hyperinflation.
evidence.source: Blanch L, et al. Measurement of air trapping, intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure, and dynamic hyperinflation in mechanically ventilated patients. Minerva Anestesiol. 2005;71(6):245-257.
